short: Henry VIII's fifth wife, Catherine Howard, was beheaded for treason following the discovery of her adulterous affairs.
full:
Catherine Howard, the teenage cousin of Anne Boleyn, married Henry VIII in July 1540, just weeks after the annulment of his marriage to Anne of Cleves. Promoted by the conservative Catholic faction led by her uncle, the Duke of Norfolk, she briefly reinvigorated the aging King. However, in late 1541, Archbishop Thomas Cranmer informed Henry of Catherine's sexual history before her marriage and her ongoing affairs during it, notably with the courtier Thomas Culpeper.

The revelations devastated the King and decisively shifted power away from the conservative faction at court. Catherine was stripped of her title as queen, and Parliament passed a bill of attainder declaring it treason for an unchaste woman to marry the King without disclosing her past. She was beheaded at the Tower of London in February 1542, along with the men accused of being her lovers.
